messages.subject: "No climate data for this site" Error
messages.subject_clean: "No climate data for this site" Error
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am attempting to extract data for lat long sites in Central America. All code runs and produces results, but I receive an error that states it is using dummy data and there is no environmental data for this site. The function still produces an output, but I am unsure if this error just corresponds to some of the variables that return "0" values, or if it has produced dummy data for all variables since this area is just not part of the micro_global set. My primary goal is to get TALOC values.

Code:

loc <- c(16.2, -90.9)
micro <- micro_global(loc = loc)

Error:
"Extracting climate data
no climate data for this site, using dummy data so solar is still produced
extracting soil moisture data
sorry, there is no environmental data for this location
running microclimate model for 12 days by 1 years at site"

Thank you very much in advance, and thank you for great tutorials and reading about this package.

Sarah

messages.subject_clean: "No climate data for this site" Error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sarah,

You'll get this if you are in the water so if you're doing sites near the coast you can have this happen because the climate layers are a bit blocky. But, in your case you've simply put the coordinates in the wrong way around.

Try
loc <- c(-90.9, 16.2) # longitude, latitude

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: using terraclimate locally
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I've made some changes to get_terra (which is used by micro_era5 and micro_ncep for climate change scenarios) and micro_terra to enable you to have the data locally. This will get around failures to connect to the data by opendap, which can be a pain if you're running a big loop. I pushed the changes to the github repository so you'll need to reinstall it with

devtools::install_github('mrke/NicheMapR')

to use these changes. I'll put it in the new release which I'll finalise late next month.

The code below will download all the data (about 86 gigs) which you should then arrange into subfolders:

data
data_plus2
data_plus4

with the historical data going into 'data'. Then you can specify the folder that these subfolders are in as the 'terra_source' parameter in micro_ncep, micro_era5 and micro_terra (and 'source' for get_terra) and it will look there to find the files.

code for downloading:
vars <- c('ppt', 'soil', 'srad', 'tmax', 'tmin', 'vap', 'ws', 'vpd')
for(year in 1958:2021){
  for(j in 1:length(vars)){
    cmd <- paste0('wget -nc -c -nd https://climate.northwestknowledge.net/TERRACLIMATE-DATA/TerraClimate_', vars[j], '_', year, '.nc')
    system(cmd)
  }
}

vars <- c('ppt', 'soil', 'srad', 'tmax', 'tmin', 'vpd')

for(year in 1985:2015){
  for(j in 1:length(vars)){
    cmd <- paste0('wget http://thredds.northwestknowledge.net:8080/thredds/fileServer/TERRACLIMATE_ALL/data_plus4C/TerraClimate_4c_', vars[j], '_', year, '.nc')
    system(cmd)
    cmd <- paste0('wget http://thredds.northwestknowledge.net:8080/thredds/fileServer/TERRACLIMATE_ALL/data_plus2C/TerraClimate_2c_', vars[j], '_', year, '.nc')
    system(cmd)
  }
}

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Extracting mean annual temperatures
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarah,

This is more of an R than an NicheMapR question, but here's how you can do it e.g. per day or per month:

loc <- c(-89.944, 15.083)

dstart <- "01/01/2008"

dfinish <-"31/12/2009"

micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)

dates <- micro$dates
metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout)

# daily
taloc.max.daily <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%d/%m/%Y")), FUN = max) # aggregate by day
colnames(taloc.max.daily) <- c('date', 'max.taloc') # change default column names from aggregate
taloc.max.daily$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.daily$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y') # change dates from character back to date format
taloc.max.daily <- taloc.max.daily[order(taloc.max.daily$date), ] # sort by date (the order got changed by aggregate)
plot(taloc.max.daily)

#monthly
taloc.max.monthly <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%m/%Y")), FUN = max)
colnames(taloc.max.monthly) <- c('date', 'max.taloc')
taloc.max.monthly$date <- paste0('15/', taloc.max.monthly$date) # extra step compared to above - pasting the middle day of each month to the date string
taloc.max.monthly$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.monthly$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y')
taloc.max.monthly <- taloc.max.monthly[order(taloc.max.monthly$date), ]
plot(taloc.max.monthly)

All the best,
Mike

Sarah

On Monday, 27 June 2022 at 18:31:41 UTC-4 NicheMapR wrote:
> Hi Sarah,
>
> This is more of an R than an NicheMapR question, but here's how you can do it e.g. per day or per month:
>
> loc <- c(-89.944, 15.083)
>
> dstart <- "01/01/2008"
>
> dfinish <-"31/12/2009"
>
> micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)
> dates <- micro$dates
> metout <- as.data.frame(micro$metout)
>
> # daily
> taloc.max.daily <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%d/%m/%Y")), FUN = max) # aggregate by day
> colnames(taloc.max.daily) <- c('date', 'max.taloc') # change default column names from aggregate
> taloc.max.daily$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.daily$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y') # change dates from character back to date format
> taloc.max.daily <- taloc.max.daily[order(taloc.max.daily$date), ] # sort by date (the order got changed by aggregate)
> plot(taloc.max.daily)
>
> #monthly
> taloc.max.monthly <- aggregate(metout$TALOC, by=list(format(dates, "%m/%Y")), FUN = max)
> colnames(taloc.max.monthly) <- c('date', 'max.taloc')
> taloc.max.monthly$date <- paste0('15/', taloc.max.monthly$date) # extra step compared to above - pasting the middle day of each month to the date string
> taloc.max.monthly$date <- as.POSIXct(taloc.max.monthly$date, format = '%d/%m/%Y')
> taloc.max.monthly <- taloc.max.monthly[order(taloc.max.monthly$date), ]
> plot(taloc.max.monthly)
>
> All the best,
> Mike
> On Monday, June 27, 2022 at 11:26:46 PM UTC+10 Sarah Dolson wrote:
> >
> > Hi all,
> >
> > I am using the micro_global dataset and interested in microniche values.
> >
> > I was wondering if there is a streamline way to calculate the mean temperature values for a site with a variable like TALOC (air temperature at local height). Ideally I am looking for the mean annual or monthly annual temperature from this site. Is there a built in function to do this without extracting the hourly info for everyday and summing it through a loop?
> >
> >
> >
> > Currently my code looks like:
> >
> > loc <- c(-89.944, 15.083)
> >
> > dstart <- "01/05/2009"
> >
> > dfinish <-"01/05/2009"
> >
> > micro <- micro_ncep(loc = loc, dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish)
> >
> >
> >
> > Thank you in advance for any help!
> >
> > Sarah
> >
> >

messages.subject: Re: Confidence interval DEB and DEB_euler
messages.body_plain:
Hi Léanne,

The model is fully deterministic so there is no error on the outputs in the 'debout' matrix. The input parameters from the 'AmP' collection <https://www.bio.vu.nl/thb/deb/deblab/add_my_pet/species_list.html> do not have confidence intervals but see here  <https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304380020301824>for how you can calculate them in the context of the DEB parameter estimation process. If you have estimates of uncertainty in your parameters (or were treating them as genetically variable, or phenotypically plastic) you could run simulations that incorporate that uncertainty and then produce outputs with means and confidence intervals.

All the best,
Mike
